newsitem.title: UK: BAe shares fall on reports of jet problems.
newsitem.headline: BAe shares fall on reports of jet problems.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc fell on Wednesday on newspaper reports that it had advised customers not to use older versions of its Hawk jet training aircraft after a problem was found with one, dealers said.
British Aerospace shares were down 15p at 1234-1/2 pence by 0901 GMT.
According to the Financial Times, a problem had been found in a component in the tail control system in a Hawk jet -- one of British Aerospace's big export success stories.
"There's a report about problems with Hawk jets and the shares are down on the back of that," one market-maker said.
A British Aerospace spokesman confirmed that a problem had been found during a routine inspection on a Royal Air Force (RAF) Hawk but said he expected the problem soon to be resolved.
"As a safety precaution and a normal practice in the aerospace industry we have advised all members of the British Aerospace Hawk fleet of the situation," he said.
"This particular unit in which we found the problem has been in service for 20 years and there have been no previous occurences."
He said Hawk jets had not been grounded by the RAF. "The RAF has recommended that the component should be inspected before flight in aircraft which have flown more than 600 hours."
